reason: This is FLOPO:0991196 crested with a degree word. 'Obscurely' (faintly) goes in the record as a qualifier, the same way 'obscure' and '±' are handled. Strictly the decision is rule:flopo_value, because the target is a FLOPO value.
A peaked ligule, aril apex or corona shoulder is one that rises to a point, which is PATO_0002258 pointed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1, place on the part: 'on the veins') with docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md; vein = vascular bundle (PO_0005020) of the bearer, quality pink (FLOPO_0988000)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins of the sepal or petal, not to the whole organ. So this is a part of the bearer with a colour, not a new value.

target: new: colour of a marking (punctate PATO_0001512 on the bearer; purple FLOPO_0988008 for the dots)
reason: Two values joined: the surface is dotted (PATO_0001512 punctate) and the dots are purple. Dots are not a PO part, so the colour of the marking needs a pattern. Until there is one, use punctate alone. One example ('densely so along veins') is a transcription fragment.

target: new: colour of a marking (spotted PATO_0000333 on the bearer; reddish brown PATO_0001287 for the spots)
reason: Same structure as 'purple punctate': the bearer is spotted and the spots have a colour of their own. 'Reddish brown' must not become the colour of the bract or glume itself.
Silky down is soft, appressed, shiny hair, which is PATO_0104358 sericeous (exact synonym 'silky'). 'Downy' only repeats that the surface is hairy. 'When young' goes to the state of the bearer.
An acute apex that narrows to a slender point. 'Slenderly' is a manner word and does not create a separate value class.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values: oblong PATO_0000946 / obovate PATO_0001936) with docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md for 'sub-'
reason: A shape between two existing shapes, with an approximating prefix. This is a pattern, not a term. The 'nectary' bearer in the 'with' list looks like a grounding error for 'lip'.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (transition between two values: rhomboid PATO_0001938 / elliptic PATO_0000947) with docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md for 'sub-'
reason: A compound of two existing shapes with an approximating prefix.

target: docs/odp/16-quality-of-a-whole-towards-its-parts.md (whole split PATO_0001786; its lobes unequal FLOPO:0991101)
reason: The calyx is divided, and its segments differ in size or depth. That is one quality of the whole and one of the set of its parts, which is pattern 16 rather than a single value.
'Stamens or sepals unequally long' means the members of a set of like parts differ in size (in length), which is FLOPO:0991101 unequal.

target: new: colour of a covering (bearded FLOPO:0991118 on the bearer; trichome PO_0000282 of the bearer white FLOPO_0988009)
reason: Barbate is already FLOPO:0991118 bearded (synonym 'barbate'), and 'white' is the colour of the hairs, not of the petal. Hairs are a PO part (trichome), so the colour can be stated of them. Until then, use bearded alone.

Widest at the middle, with both ends alike, is how the Manual of Leaf Architecture defines elliptic (character 10, the medial class). Records with a second shape in the same sentence should keep that shape as well.
It states that a lamella is absent, but 'lamella' is a generic part with no PO or FLOPO class, and 'wing' is itself a generic part. An absence can only be stated once the part has a class.
This is the absence of a part, the opposite of 'stoloniferous' (stolon present).

The branches are borne in clusters from about the same point. That is FLOPO:0991098 fascicled, said of the branches (branch PO_0025073) of the stem or plant. The branching itself is PATO_0000402 branched.

target: docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md (2 locules, 'locular' in flora_counted_parts.tsv) with a qualifier for the incomplete septum
reason: In Astragalus the pod is partly divided into two locules by an incomplete false septum. That is a count of locules with a qualifier, not a new quality. 'semibi¬locular' is the same word with a hyphenation artefact.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (filaments inserted on the disc lobes)
reason: In Tamarix (Baum's disc types), 'epilophic' means the filaments arise from the tops of the disc lobes. It is a relation between filament and disc lobe, used in a single genus, so it is not a general value.
Same reading as 'widest at mid-blade'. Unlike the bare 'broadest' rejected earlier, this phrase says where the widest part is.
A variant spelling of heterostylous. It should be added as a synonym of FLOPO:0991137.
A truncated fragment ('cleaving up' into fibres or strips?) describing how the bulb tunics break. Without the rest of the phrase it cannot be told apart from fissured, fibrous or split.
'Expanded' maps to PATO_0001571 dilated (C181), and 'scarcely' (escasamente) almost negates it. 'In fruit' goes to the stage. The Spanish examples are the same statement.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) of the distal leaf lamina; quality width (PATO_0000921) as a bounded measurement (docs/odp/02-bounded-measurement.md)
reason: A moss measurement: the bearer is the laminal cells in the distal part of the leaf, and the quality is ordinary width. Two of the examples have lost the bearer and should not be read as leaf width.
A costa that ends at the leaf apex, not beyond it, matches the definition of FLOPO:0991163 percurrent. 'Shortly excurrent' in the alternatives is FLOPO:0991162.
The laminal or testal cells are rectangular and longer than wide. 'Elongate' can be added as PATO_0001154 elongated, or left as a modifier.

label: metallic
definition: A glistening quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface reflecting light with a metal-like sheen.
reason: It cannot be negated 'glistening': a surface can shine without a metallic sheen. All six statements are negated ('without ... when dry'), so they would be rule:negated_value of this class plus the specimen condition (pattern 06). Rejecting is also reasonable while it is only ever used in negation.
The peristome segments are perforate. The holes are not a PO part, so their ovate shape cannot be stated of them and is lost.

Haplostemonous means the stamens are in a single whorl, which is uniseriate said of the androecium, not of the flower. The usual equal number of stamens and petals can be a count (pattern 03) if a flora states it.
French for 'in several series', said of involucral bracts; this is multiseriate. The 'seed' and 'flower' bearers are grounding errors for the involucre.
'Non mûres' is the state of the fruit or seed being described, not a phenotype. It belongs with the context words 'immature' and 'ripe', and it should be added to config/flora_context_words.tsv.
